name: OOP Interview Mastery: Output Prediction, Pitfalls, and Tracing
subject: Object-Oriented Programming Systems

mcqs.question: Why can constructors NOT be declared `virtual` in C++?
options: Because constructors return a pointer rather than a reference
Because an object’s vptr and vtable link are not established until its constructor runs
Because constructors are always executed on the GPU
Because virtual methods must be declared outside the class body
mcqs.explanation: To dispatch a virtual function, the object must already exist and have a valid vptr pointing to its vtable. Before constructor execution, no such structure exists.

mcqs.question: In C++, if a base class has a virtual function `virtual void foo(int a = 10)`, and derived overrides it as `void foo(int a = 20) override`, what value is passed when calling `basePtr->foo()`?
options: Compilation error: default parameters cannot be overridden
mcqs.explanation: Default arguments are resolved statically at compile time based on the pointer type (Base, which has 10), while the function body is resolved dynamically (Derived). The derived function executes with 10!
